top_news.title: Comparing Transformers and Hybrid Models at the Token Level
top_news.dek: Researchers analyze the performance differences between pure Transformers and hybrid models using Olmo 3 and Olmo Hybrid weights.
top_news.brief: This study investigates why hybrid language models—which combine attention and recurrent layers—often outperform pure Transformers. By examining open-weight models, the authors aim to isolate the specific data and architectural capabilities that drive these performance gains, testing whether empirical improvements align with theoretical advantages in state tracking.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the architectural comparison between Transformer and hybrid model layers.

top_news.title: AWS Previews FinOps Agent for Cost Analysis and Optimization
top_news.dek: AWS has launched a public preview of its FinOps Agent to automate cost anomaly detection and resource spend correlation.
top_news.brief: The AWS FinOps Agent is a managed service designed to streamline cloud financial management. It automates the investigation of cost anomalies and correlates spending fluctuations with specific AWS activity. The tool integrates with Slack and Jira to route findings directly to the relevant resource owners.

top_news.title: Show HN: Adrafinil – keep a lid-closed Mac awake only while agents work
top_news.dek: Adrafinil is a new utility that prevents Mac systems from sleeping only while AI coding agents are actively running.
top_news.brief: This utility helps developers manage power settings by keeping a Mac awake specifically during AI agent tasks. It is designed to prevent the system from entering sleep mode while long-running coding processes are active, ensuring uninterrupted workflows.

top_news.title: Liquid AI Ships LFM2.5-230M with llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX Support for On-Device Inference
top_news.dek: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-230M, a compact 230M-parameter model optimized for on-device inference and tool use.
top_news.brief: The LFM2.5-230M model supports llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX. It demonstrates high performance on edge hardware, achieving 213 tokens per second on a Galaxy S25 Ultra. It is specifically tuned for instruction following, data extraction, and tool-use tasks, outperforming larger models in its class.

top_news.dek: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark introduces million-token context intelligence for highly efficient long-context processing.
top_news.brief: The DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark model focuses on scaling context windows to one million tokens. It is released under an MIT license and is available via Hugging Face, targeting applications that require deep reasoning over massive datasets.

primary.title: DeepSeek Releases DSpark, a Speculative Decoding Framework That Accelerates DeepSeek-V4 Per-User Generation 60–85% Over MTP-1
primary.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DSpark, a speculative decoding framework that attaches a draft module to existing DeepSeek-V4 weights. It pairs a parallel draft backbone with a lightweight Markov head to cut suffix decay, then adds confidence-scheduled verification that tailors how many tokens get checked to real-time GPU load. Offline, accepted length rises 16–31% over DFlash and Eagle3; in production it speeds per-user generation 57–85% over the MTP-1 baseline, losslessly. The training repo, DeepSpec, ships under MIT.
